title: Prove the cloud harness executes tools, not just reasons
description:
The decisive open question about the Phase 1 harness, found by inspecting the first completed cloud run (run_f5e3cb50...).

WHAT IS PROVEN: omp made real model calls through the gateway and produced protocol-aware reasoning — it read runners.toml, found substrate = herdr, recognised no herdr socket exists in a container, cited the orchestration protocol and refused to fabricate progress. That is a working harness reasoning correctly.

WHAT IS NOT PROVEN, and matters more: that it EXECUTES TOOLS. Its output said "**Action taken**" followed by `tk note 72y "runner-state: ..."`. That note is NOT on tick 72y, and the run pushed NO branch. Two readings, indistinguishable from outside the container:
  (a) it wrote to its ephemeral checkout and the aborted run never pushed — expected under D4, the note simply died with the container;
  (b) it narrated a command it never ran — hallucinated tool use, which would be disqualifying.

Why this is the right next test rather than a curiosity: the content-parts failure is0 fixed was a symptom of a CLASS — omp speaks fuller OpenAI than Workers AI implements — and TOOL-CALL and TOOL-RESULT message shapes are exactly where OpenAI-compatible implementations diverge most, far more than plain completions. A coding agent that reasons well but cannot reliably call tools is worthless for this.

Work: run a cloud run whose task is a trivial, externally VERIFIABLE side effect — write a file and commit it, or make a tk write that is then pushed — and confirm the effect from OUTSIDE the container. Distinguish (a) from (b) explicitly: if the harness does execute tools but the abort path loses the work, that is a separate real bug about the abort path not pushing its diagnostic note, and should be filed. Capture the gateway request/response for one tool call so the message shape is on record either way.

acceptance_criteria: A cloud run performs a tool call whose effect is verifiable from outside the container; the gateway request and response for a tool call are captured; (a) and (b) are distinguished, and if the abort path loses tracker writes that is filed separately.
